name: St. Ulrich am Pillersee
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village by Pillersee with crystal-clear waters and breathtaking mountain views.
beschreibung:
Überblick

St. Ulrich am Pillersee is situated in the idyllic Pillerseetal valley in the north-eastern Tyrolean district of Kitzbühel at an elevation of 847 metres above sea level, nestled along the eastern and southern shores of the emerald-green Pillersee. Framed by the rugged limestone precipices of the Loferer Steinberge and Ulrichshörner to the east and the gentle ridge of the Buchensteinwand to the west, this municipality of around 1,900 inhabitants is among the most scenic retreats in the Kitzbühel Alps. The village is characterised by an authentic, family-friendly ambience: crystalline alpine waters, peaceful lakeside promenades, fragrant mountain pine forests, and an impeccably maintained network of hiking trails and cross-country ski tracks make St. Ulrich a haven of tranquillity and outdoor recreation.

Geschichte

The settlement of the Pillerseetal valley is intimately linked with Bavarian monastic foundations during the High Middle Ages. In 1073, Count Rapoto donated the valley and church to the Benedictine monastery of Rott am Inn ('Bileresse per totum cum ecclesia'), which held manorial authority and maintained a local priory until the secularisation of 1803. The parish church, dedicated to Saint Ulrich of Augsburg, was completed in Gothic style in 1506 and features a distinctive double-onion dome. At the northern end of the lake stands the fortified pilgrimage church of St. Adolari dating from 1407, housing North Tyrol's most significant Gothic fresco cycle depicting the life of the Virgin Mary. In the 19th century, St. Ulrich achieved international acclaim through mountain pine oil distillation: in 1856, pharmacist Mathias Mack identified the therapeutic properties of dwarf pine oil; the Mack brothers subsequently established the world's oldest mountain pine distillery in St. Ulrich, preserving this artisan craft to this day.

Anreise

By car, St. Ulrich am Pillersee is reached from the west via the Inntal motorway A12 (Wörgl-Ost exit) along the Loferer Bundesstraße B178 through St. Johann in Tirol and Fieberbrunn, where the Pillersee-Landesstraße (L2) leads straight to the lake. From the north, travel toll-free via Kufstein, Ellmau, and St. Johann or via Inzell, Lofer, and Waidring. Rail travellers access the regional stations of Fieberbrunn or Hochfilzen on the Salzburg-Tyrol railway or the express station at St. Johann in Tirol. VVT regional bus service 8302 connects Kitzbühel, St. Johann, Fieberbrunn, St. Ulrich, and Waidring at regular intervals; holidaymakers travel free of charge on regional buses using the PillerseeTal guest card.

Tipps

The crown jewel of any stay is lake Pillersee itself: formed by a prehistoric rockslide, this 24-hectare natural lake invites visitors for refreshing swimming, stand-up paddleboarding, and rowing, accompanied by a scenic, ten-kilometre circuit trail around its shores. Directly along the waterfront, the Kneipp facility filled with ice-cold mountain spring water provides soothing revitalization. A fascinating heritage highlight is the historic Mack mountain pine distillery, complete with copper stills, an alpine botanical garden, and an informative museum. Art aficionados must visit the pilgrimage church of St. Adolari to admire its 15th-century frescoes. Furthermore, an excursion up the neighbouring Buchensteinwand (1,456 m) brings you to the 30-metre-tall Jakobskreuz, the world's largest accessible summit cross with panoramic viewing platforms.
